Question B-002-003-001.

Why the correct answer is right: A routine voice CQ is a short general call: call CQ, say “this is,” and identify with your call sign so any station can answer.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Say \"CQ\" once, followed by \"this is,\" followed by your call sign spoken three times": Saying CQ only once may be missed; the taught routine uses a short repeated CQ before identification.
- sourceIndex 2: "Say \"CQ\" at least five times, followed by \"this is,\" followed by your call sign spoken once": Five or more CQs followed by one call sign is unnecessarily long and gives less balanced identification.
- sourceIndex 3: "Say \"CQ\" at least ten times, followed by \"this is,\" followed by your call sign spoken once": Ten or more CQs wastes airtime and is not the concise voice calling pattern.
